articleBody:
Before your tile installer arrives to start setting your bathroom floor, checking off key site preparations keeps the project running on schedule and avoids costly surprises.

- [ ] Measure total square footage and add a 10% to 15% waste allowance — Having extra tiles on site accounts for cuts around plumbing pipes, heating registers, and future repairs.
- [ ] Inspect existing subfloor for squeaks, bouncy spots, or water stains — Any soft, sagging, or water-damaged subfloor must be reinforced before new underlayment goes down.
- [ ] Confirm your chosen tile has a wet slip-resistance rating suitable for bathrooms — Smooth, glossy finishes become dangerously slick when wet, so textured or matte surfaces work best for floors.
- [ ] Purchase transition strips compatible with adjoining hallway floor heights — Adding underlayment and tile changes the finished floor height and requires clean doorway transitions.
- [ ] Ensure toilet, vanity base, and baseboards are scheduled for removal — Floor tile should sit underneath the toilet and vanity footprint rather than being cut awkwardly around them.
- [ ] Verify that backer boards or uncoupling membranes match the mortar specs — Mixing incompatible brands of thinset, membranes, and substrates can void manufacturer warranties.
- [ ] Confirm proper under-door clearance with the new finished floor height — A higher finished floor might rub against the bathroom door, requiring trimming of the door slab.
- [ ] Clear a dedicated, dry staging area for tile boxes, wet saws, and mortar mixing — Installers need a clear, protected space nearby to mix thinset and execute precision cuts safely.

How to use this checklist:
Review these items with your general contractor during your pre-construction walk-through. Addressing framing rigidity, moisture history, and height transitions early prevents delays on install day.
